commitResults.messageTitle: Update AboutUs page with my details
commitResults.messageBody: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

build.gradle declared JavaFX as raw implementation dependencies for
win/mac/linux all at once, with no plugin managing platform selection.
This makes the main run/test/debug classpath ambiguous about which
platform's native library to load - it can pick the wrong one (e.g.
loading javafx-graphics-win.jar on macOS), causing "Error initializing
QuantumRenderer: no suitable pipeline found" / "No toolkit found" when
running or debugging locally. It's non-deterministic: which platform
gets picked can vary between runs (observed directly - same machine,
same code, one run worked and the next picked the Windows jar).

Fix:
- Add the org.openjfx.javafxplugin with a javafx {} block, so the main
  classpath resolves via Gradle's attribute-based variant matching to
  the one correct host-platform variant - no ambiguity.
- Move the "bundle every platform for the fat jar" dependencies out of
  the main classpath entirely, into one configuration per platform
  (OpenJFX marks same-module different-classifier artifacts as
  conflicting capabilities, so they can't share one configuration).
  shadowJar now pulls from all of them in addition to the normal
  runtimeClasspath.

Verified: 3 consecutive `./gradlew run` launches, all correct and
clean (previously flaky). Full test suite + checkstyle pass. The
shadow jar still bundles all platforms (54 .dll + 7 .dylib + 11 .so,
same as before this change).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add applicant ID, interview notes, years of experience and source
commitResults.messageBody:
Extend Applicant with the details a recruiter needs to assess candidates:
- ApplicantId: a UUID generated on creation and kept across edits. It is
  an internal identifier, so it is excluded from equals and hashCode.
- InterviewNotes (i/), Source (s/): optional free text.
- YearsOfExperience (y/): optional whole number from 0 to 60.
Skills reuse the existing tags (t/).

add and edit accept the new prefixes; an empty value is allowed and
clears the field on edit. JSON storage reads and writes the new fields,
and files written before they existed still load. The applicant card and
sample data show the new fields.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Implement ComparisonState as a concrete class
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the ComparisonState interface with a class that holds the pending
ComparisonPair, or none, with a read-only observable property for the UI.
setCurrentPair rejects a pair whose applicants have no record in the
ApplicantRegistry and leaves the current pair unchanged. Membership in the
comparison list stays with ComparisonList, which avoids a circular dependency.

Add equals, hashCode and toString to ComparisonPair, which ComparisonState
needs to compare pairs and to avoid change events for an unchanged pair.

Closes #68

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Implement ComparisonState as a concrete class

commitResults.messageTitle: Show the current comparison pair in the comparison panel
commitResults.messageBody:
RecruitDexData now owns the ComparisonState, which Model exposes and Logic
passes to the UI as an observable property, together with the list of all
applicant records.

ComparisonPanel shows the two applicants of the current pair, labelled A and
B, looked up by ID so that edits to their records appear straight away.
With no pair, or a pair whose record is missing, the card shows an empty
state. Resetting the data clears the pending pair, since it refers to the old
records.

Closes #69

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
